why: MI-280 unit U9. A docs-only change: one `updates` entry on BL-20260911-THE-CONSTRAINT-READOUT-CRON-NOW-CLEARS-ITS-SELF-TEST-AND-DIES-ON-SESSION-BRIEF-GUARD. No code. Tier-1, docs/ only. WHY A REPRODUCTION IS THE DELIVERABLE RATHER THAN A FIX: the row demands it in terms — 'Whoever takes this REPRODUCES it before choosing one. Naming a cause off this evidence would be the unprovenanced-diagnostic class this repo has a guard for.' Two candidate causes were indistinguishable from its evidence and have DIFFERENT fixes, so a fix chosen before the reproduction would have had a coin-flip chance of leaving the row open while looking closed. CAUSE (i), A RENDERER/GUARD DISAGREEMENT: REFUTED. On an untouched origin/main the guard exits 0, and running the workflow's own sequence (constraint_readout.py --write, then render_session_brief.py --write, which changes CLAUDE.md + CONSTRAINT.json + READOUT.md) and then the guard immediately against an unmoved base also exits 0. CAUSE (ii), THE BRIEF GOING STALE AGAINST A MOVING BASE: REPRODUCED, with the workflow's exact failure. Rendering at origin/main~12 and then advancing only the registers to current main — which is what GitHub's MERGE REF does, since PR checks run against branch-merged-with-main — produces `verdict=introduced_registers_changed` and exit 1, the same guard, verdict class and exit as #11789's failing `guards` run. AND THE PART THAT WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY KNOWN: the existing remedy CANNOT reach this. commit-to-main's one-shot stale-branch refresh merges main in to re-trigger the checks, and it never RE-RENDERS the derived file — so even when it fires it mints a new sha carrying the same stale brief and the same guard fails again. For a producer whose output is DERIVED FROM the registers, re-running the checks is not the remedy; re-deriving is. THE FIX IS PROPOSED PRECISELY AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, and the reasons are stated rather than implied: a `refresh-command` input on commit-to-main would be PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION (the refresh fires once, a third of the way in, so a base moving after it leaves the brief stale again); the complete answer is a DESIGN CHOICE nobody has made — re-derive on every poll, or have the guard evaluate against the merge BASE, or stop having producers render the brief — and picking one is not a lane's call; and the file is LANDING_MACHINERY, so it would be a fourth `landing: hold` PR behind three already queued for a human merge. Weakening session-brief-guard as a side effect of unblocking a cron is exactly the change that should be chosen deliberately. IT CLEARS NOTHING AND DOES NOT CLAIM TO: the row's criterion is a SCHEDULED run concluding success with CONSTRAINT.json on main carrying that run's stamp. Nothing here is a run. The row stays open with its cause established and one candidate eliminated.
